issues.title: Missing accuracy dependence in the spectral-radius theorem's sparsity condition

failure_location.quote: Note $\kappa_V(A)=\kappa_V((n/\delta)M+N)$ so Theorem \ref{a1} means with high probability that

issues.failure_explanation: Applying a1 with deterministic part (n/delta)M requires n rho of order log(n) times log(n+n||M||/delta). The spectral-radius theorem assumes only dependence on log(n+||M||), so for an admissibly tiny delta its invocation of a1 is outside a1's stated hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem does not establish its claimed backward-error guarantee uniformly for every delta in (0,1) at the stated sparsity and runtime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the theorem's sparsity premise by the condition actually required when applying a1 to the scaled matrix: nρ ≥ C log(n) log(n+n‖M‖/δ). State that the runtime and guarantee apply only to parameter pairs satisfying this condition, or choose ρ accordingly. The remainder of the power-method argument can then be retained.
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and requires no new proof architecture, but it introduces substantive accuracy dependence into the sparsity and runtime contract. For fixed sparse ρ it withdraws the guarantee for sufficiently small δ, so it is not a routine technical qualification or typo. The resulting theorem remains recognizably comparable, making the loss limited rather than major.

issues.title: Undefined input in the spectral-radius theorem

failure_location.quote: there is an algorithm $\alg{specr}(A)$ which computes a value such that

issues.failure_explanation: The formal statement fixes M but invokes the algorithm on A and compares with the radius of A+E without quantifying A. The earlier global convention A=M+N_g does not resolve this because the proof resets A=M+(delta/n)N. Consequently, the theorem does not define a consistent input, internal perturbation, and nearby output matrix.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's algorithmic input-output contract is ill-defined even before its separate probabilistic and sparsity-hypothesis defects are considered.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use M consistently for the external input and reserve a new symbol, say Ã=M+(δ/n)N, for the internally perturbed matrix. Write the algorithm as specr(M) and state its estimate equivalently for spr(Ã) or spr(M+E), with E=Ã−M; make the same relabeling throughout the proof.
issues.why_classification: The old proof uniquely determines the roles of M and the internally sampled perturbation. Consistent relabeling produces the intended mixed backward-error contract without changing the algorithm, any inference, or any mathematical guarantee. The defect is therefore a transcriptional naming inconsistency.

issues.title: Omitted success probability in the spectral-radius theorem

failure_location.quote: there is an algorithm $\alg{specr}(A)$ which computes a value such that

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theorem \ref{a1} means with high probability that

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem presents its approximation and perturbation inequalities without any success event. The proof establishes the norm comparison only on an event of probability at least 1-1/n and obtains the condition-number bound on another high-probability event. Their intersection supports only a randomized high-probability conclusion, not the unqualified statement.
issues.overall_effect: No deterministic or every-sample spectral-radius guarantee is proved; only a high-probability guarantee is supported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that the displayed approximation and backward-error guarantee holds with high probability over both N and b. Intersect the event from a1 with the Gaussian-vector norm-comparison event, giving, for example, success probability at least 1−1/n−O(n^{-K}), with any other explicitly used high-probability event included by the same union bound.
issues.why_classification: The procedure is visibly randomized and the proof already establishes the required component events. Adding their intersection as the theorem's success event is a short, routine repair that preserves the method, conclusion, approximation factor, runtime, and intended randomized guarantee.

issues.title: Missing epsilon in the pseudospectral tail radial factor
issues.failure_explanation: Polar integration gives 2 pi times the integral from R+epsilon of r Pr(r-epsilon<||M+N||) dr. Setting x=r-epsilon changes r to x+epsilon. The old integral with factor x therefore underestimates the tail and does not follow from the preceding line.
issues.overall_effect: The tail estimate in a20 is not derived, independently leaving a gap in a20 and in the formal results that consume its pseudospectral-area bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the polar tail integral set r=x+ε, obtaining 2π∫_R^∞(x+ε)Pr(x<‖M+N‖)dx, and carry x+ε through the subsequent norm-tail estimate. One may state the harmless scale condition ε≤R used downstream, under which the added term is absorbed by a constant-factor change in the subgaussian tail bound.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine invalid change-of-variables step rather than mere notation, but the correction and tail check are short and routine. In the scales used by a1, the extra ε changes only constants, so the pseudospectral estimate and all listed downstream rates and guarantees remain unchanged.

issues.title: Incorrect inner-disk area in the pseudospectral bound
issues.failure_explanation: After splitting at |z|=R+epsilon, the integral over the inner disk is at most its supremum times pi(R+epsilon)^2. It is neither equal to nor bounded by pi R^2 times that supremum for unrestricted epsilon.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a20's displayed area estimate is not proved, leaving the pseudospectral-area input to a1 and its spectral-radius application unestablished until corrected. The distinct tail-substitution error is represented by C09.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the integral over |z|≤R+ε by π(R+ε)^2 times the displayed supremum, changing the equality to an upper bound as appropriate. Propagate this prefactor through a20 and its consumers; in the downstream regime ε≤R it is at most a constant multiple of R^2.
issues.why_classification: The old area estimate is an invalid inference, so it is not purely typographical. Nevertheless, the geometrically forced correction is local and requires no new lemma or construction, and it changes only an inessential constant in every recorded downstream application.

issues.title: Invalid common-center inference for an eigenvalue pair

failure_location.quote: there must be some $z\in\net$ such that $\lambda_i,\lambda_j\in\ball(z,r)$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\net$ be an $r$-net of the disk of radius $R$.

issues.failure_explanation: For eigenvalues at distance at most r, their midpoint is at distance at most r/2 from each. An r-net may place its nearest center as far as r from that midpoint, yielding distances as large as 3r/2, so the asserted common radius-r ball does not follow. A covering radius r/2 is required.
issues.overall_effect: The union bound and coefficient in a21 are unsupported, so the eigenvalue-gap input to a1 and the dependent spectral-radius theorem are unestablished until the net geometry is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an r/2-net of the disk, for example a maximal r/2-net with centers inside the disk. The midpoint of two eigenvalues separated by at most r is then within r/2 of a center, so both eigenvalues lie in its radius-r ball. Replace the covering-number coefficient by the corresponding universal constant times (R/r)^2 and retain the same union-bound argument.
issues.why_classification: The common-center assertion is a real geometric gap, but halving the covering radius repairs it by a standard local net argument. Only an absolute covering constant changes, leaving the singular-value exponents, eigenvalue-gap rate, and all dependent guarantees intact.

issues.title: Missing domain restriction on the singular-value index

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $B_1$ has $m+1$ rows and $B_2$ has $n-m-1$ rows.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement quantifies every nonnegative m, but sigma_{n-m} is not a defined singular value when m is at least n, and the proof then asks for a block with n-m-1 rows. Thus those stated cases are not admissible mathematical inputs.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a16 overstates its domain. Its actual downstream uses at m=0 and m=1 remain within the corrected domain and do not depend on the invalid cases.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace m∈Z_{≥0} by 0≤m<n (with m integral) in a16. No proof change is needed for those admissible indices.
issues.why_classification: Both σ_{n−m} and the stated block dimensions uniquely force m<n, while the omitted cases are not coherent mathematical inputs. The correction removes no meaningful promise, and the recorded uses m=0 and m=1 remain unchanged.

issues.title: Invalid level-count equality after rounding

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Round the real and imaginary parts of all other entries \textit{up} to the nearest multiple of $\frac1{2\sqrt n}\cdot t^{k+1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: A coordinate between the (k+1)st and kth thresholds is retained and rounded. That rounding can move it across the kth threshold, so a_k(v) need not equal a_k(tilde v). The valid bookkeeping tracks a_k(v) below a_k(tilde v) and a_{k+1}(v) above it when the thresholds decrease.
issues.overall_effect: The stated net partition and its support-cardinality justification in a18 do not follow as written; a19 and the formal results downstream of a19 therefore inherit the gap. The independent entropy-decay defect is separately represented by C12.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false equality by a_k(v)≤a_k(ṽ)≤a_{k+1}(ṽ)=a_{k+1}(v). Keeping j=a_k(ṽ), use the selected level ratio to obtain a_{k+1}(v)=|supp(ṽ)|≤H a_k(v)≤Hj, where H=(log(2/s)/ρ)^{1/K}. This supplies the same support-cardinality bound and permits the existing net partition after routine bookkeeping adjustments.
issues.why_classification: Rounding genuinely invalidates the asserted equality, so some mathematical checking is necessary. The weaker inequalities nevertheless supply exactly the lower count and support upper bound needed by the subsequent probability and entropy estimates. The repair is short and local and does not alter any downstream statement or rate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: a_{k}(v) \le a_{k}(\tilde v) \le a_{k+1}(\tilde v) = a_{k+1}(v).

issues.title: Loss of all decay for the first support class

failure_location.quote: By combining this with (\ref{a32}), applying union bound over $k, j$, and using the second hypothesis of the lemma we obtain the desired result.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation a32 bounds the row probability by max((1-rho)^{j-1},1/2)^n. Since the subsequent union includes j=1, this upper bound equals 1 for that class. Multiplication by the nontrivial net cardinality and summation over k,j therefore cannot imply exp(-n rho/2), contrary to the final sentence of the proof.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a18's claimed compressible-vector probability bound is not proved; consequently a19, a1, and the spectral-radius theorem lose this input independently of the rounding-equality defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate the first support class before applying a32 and retain the pre-relaxation estimate [(1−ρ)+ρ/2]^n≤exp(−ρn/2). Rebalance the entropy condition by a fixed constant so the first-class net cardinality consumes only part of this decay, and redo the union bound to obtain exp(−cρn) for some absolute c>0. Equivalently, use a two-regime small-ball estimate that combines sparse-support decay with the much stronger Gaussian small-ball bound. Propagate exp(−cρn) through a19, a1, and the spectral-radius application.
issues.why_classification: A mere edit cannot recover the claimed union bound because the bound used in the old proof is exactly one for j=1 and leaves no decay to offset the net entropy. A contained but nontrivial case analysis and entropy rebalancing can restore exponential-in-nρ decay, after which only constants in the downstream high-probability bounds change. Thus no global architecture or major mathematical loss is necessary, but the work exceeds a routine local repair.

issues.title: Unmet parameter synthesis in the bottom-singular-value proposition

failure_location.quote: We obtain the final result by a union bound.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma a18 requires s at least 2^{3(K+1)} epsilon^2 n^2 R^{2K}/rho^K. For m=0, Lemma a16 then contributes n s, at least 2^{3(K+1)} epsilon^2 n^3 R^{2K}/rho^K, whereas a19 claims only epsilon^2 n^3 R^{2K}. Moreover, a18 supplies exp(-rho n/2), not a19's exp(-rho n). Thus the cited lemmas cannot yield a19 under its stated parameter map.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition a19's singular-value estimate is unproved, so the bottom-singular-value input to a1 and the spectral-radius theorem depending on a1 are also unestablished.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose and verify an explicit feasible value of s rather than asserting the final union bound. Direct use of a18 requires the incompressible contribution to include the factor [2^{3(K+1)}n^3R^{2K}ε^2/ρ^K]^{m+1} and the compressible error to be exp(−cρn), together with a scale and sparsity range satisfying both hypotheses of a18. Reoptimize K and the spectral scales in a1 to absorb 2^{O(K)}ρ^{−K} into (nR)^{O(K)}. A contained alternative is the revised parameter lemma with s=8R^{2K}n^{2(K+1)}ε^2, yielding a comparable shattering theorem at polylogarithmically stronger sparsity; the same reductions can then restate the dependent spectral-radius result under that condition.
issues.why_classification: Resolving the mismatch requires genuine parameter synthesis, a corrected singular-value proposition, and renewed downstream exponent bookkeeping; simply changing a constant is insufficient. This work remains confined to the compressible/incompressible estimate and its parameter propagation, and it preserves the ε powers, exponential probability form, and a recognizably comparable near-linear-sparsity theorem, possibly with adjusted polylogarithmic sparsity and exponents. Hence a complete nonglobal, nonmajor-loss route exists, but it is nontrivial.
